annotations.text:
The Desk on a phone — a separate installable app from the shop.

It reuses the Desk's own system exactly: ground #101312, one ink in four steps, and the rule that colour is ONLY ever state. There is no brand accent here, so the active tab is ink rather than red — a coloured tab would say something needs you when nothing does.

This is the screen the port exists for.

DeskTable is minWidth 1100 — nearly three of these screens. Every board table becomes a stack of cards instead: reference and status on one line, who and how much on the next, date last. Nothing scrolls sideways.

The lens switch stays one level above the status chips, as on desktop: it changes the data source, not the slice.

🚨 The line picker is the safety rail, not a convenience.

Money is per-LINE. Fully refunding a consolidated carrier line while its siblings are still held is refused by the server, in an order nobody can predict from this screen — so there is no "refund the order" button anywhere, on any surface.

The confirm restates the act in words: who, how much, what follows, and what stays untouched. The dialog clears z-index 60 so the tab bar cannot paint over the tap that commits money.

Usernames only on anything scannable. The real name and the ID document sit behind a deliberate reveal, one per document.

The bank check is labelled as done by hand, because it is — nothing here should imply an automated verification that is not live yet.

The honest mark is the point of this screen.

Twenty legacy routes are only PARTLY covered: the drawer moved to the Desk, the browsable register mostly did not. A row that opens the old panel says so, rather than looking native and then not being.

That list shrinks as the cutover proceeds — it should never be quietly hidden.
